Modern.tagline: One material. Fully recyclable. Gone in the recycling, not the landfill.
Modern.brandDescription: Monoflute is a sustainable, compostable packaging startup that ships mono-material mailers and boxes engineered to pass through a single curbside recycling stream. Every Monoflute pack is one substrate end to end — no mixed laminates, no plastic windows, no foil — so it actually gets recycled instead of contaminating the bale. Monoflute sells to climate-forward D2C brands that have made packaging part of their sustainability claim and need receipts to back it.
Modern.scope: Direct-to-brand sales of compostable mailers, corrugated boxes, and curbside-recyclable void fill, with stock SKUs and low-MOQ custom print. Monoflute does not run a retail storefront or sell single units to consumers.
Modern.brandNameRationale: A flute is the wavy corrugated medium glued between linerboards (A/B/C/E flute), and mono- signals single-material construction. Monoflute fuses the corrugate trade term with the mono-material recyclability promise.
Modern.industrySummary: 2025 packaging is being reshaped by Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) fees rolling out across California (SB 54), Oregon, Colorado and the EU's PPWR, which price producers on the recyclability of what they ship. Mono-material design has become the dominant compliance strategy because mixed laminates and PE-lined fiber fail material-recovery-facility sortation. PFAS bans on food-contact fiber (effective in a dozen US states by 2025) have also pushed compostable certifiers toward cleaner barrier chemistries. The opening is a brand that builds the single-stream guarantee into its name.
Modern.competitorLandscape: EcoEnclose (ecoenclose.com) leads recycled and recyclable shipping supplies with deep stock breadth. noissue (noissue.co) owns the compostable custom-print tier with a soft, design-led aesthetic. Sway (swaythefuture.com) pioneers seaweed-based replacements for plastic film. Monoflute differs by making single-stream mono-material verification the entire product story — every SKU ships with its recycling stream named on the pack.
Modern.positioningStatement: Monoflute is the packaging brand that guarantees one material per pack so it actually gets recycled.
Modern.positioningRationale: Most 'eco' packaging fails at the sortation line because it mixes fiber, plastic and foil. By committing to a single substrate per SKU, Monoflute moves the claim from intention to verifiable outcome. That guarantee is the differentiator procurement and sustainability leads can defend.

targetAudience.primary: Sustainability and operations leads at venture-backed D2C brands (skincare, apparel, supplements) who have publicly committed to recyclable packaging and need a supplier whose materials survive a real MRF. They buy in 5k-50k unit runs, audit material composition, and want documentation they can publish.

Modern.tagline: Mailers and boxes that earn the unboxing.

The Laydown sells custom-printed mailers, shipping boxes and tissue in fast, low-MOQ runs with a press-ready die-line editor that lets a founder go from artwork to proof in a browser. It is opinionated about the unboxing moment — registration-tight print, full-bleed interiors, and finishes that photograph well.
Modern.scope: Online custom packaging configurator covering mailer boxes, shipping boxes, poly-free mailers, tissue and tape, with self-serve proofing and short lead times. The Laydown serves brands, not enterprise corrugated procurement.
Modern.brandNameRationale: The laydown (or knockout) is the flat printed sheet before it is folded and glued into a box — the moment all the artwork is visible at once. It names the brand after the exact view that matters to a designer.
Modern.industrySummary: E-commerce parcel volume has normalized post-2021 but the unboxing-experience economy has hardened into a real category, with brands budgeting for tissue, inserts and full-interior print as a retention lever. Short-run digital corrugated printing (HP PageWide, inkjet single-pass) collapsed minimum order quantities, letting small brands buy 100-unit custom runs that used to require 5,000. At the same time PPWR and right-sizing mandates penalize oversized boxes, so dimensional efficiency now sells alongside aesthetics. The opening is a fast, design-first configurator that respects the die-line.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Packlane (packlane.com) is the design-forward custom-box benchmark with a strong browser editor. Arka (arka.com) competes on speed and low MOQs for D2C mailers. Fantastapack (fantastapack.com) plays the fast custom-corrugated peer. The Laydown differs by centering the press-ready laydown view and giving designers true full-bleed interior control with a real proof, not a render.

Crashlock pairs a structural picker (mailer, shipper, crash-lock base, reverse tuck) with on-demand digital print so a brand keeps a permanent 'pack profile' and triggers reruns in a click. It is the packaging back end for brands that want a repeatable, ownable box without holding a warehouse of inventory.
Modern.scope: A SaaS-style platform for designing, storing and reordering custom packaging across standard structural styles, with print-on-demand fulfillment and reorder automation. Crashlock is not a one-off custom shop; it is built for repeat ordering.
Modern.brandNameRationale: A crash-lock base (auto-bottom) is a structural die-line that pops into a locked, load-bearing base in one motion — fast and repeatable. The name signals structural fluency and one-motion reordering.
Modern.industrySummary: Custom packaging has shifted from project-based ordering to platform-based reordering as brands standardize their packaging stack and want it stored, versioned and reorderable like a digital asset. Print-on-demand corrugated has made it economical to skip large inventory holds and produce closer to demand, reducing the dead stock that EPR fees now make expensive. Structural die-line libraries (FEFCO standards plus custom) let non-engineers pick load-rated boxes confidently. The opening is a platform that treats your packaging like a saved, versioned profile.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Packlane (packlane.com) offers saved designs but is order-led rather than profile-led. Arka (arka.com) emphasizes fast reorders and a clean dashboard. Fantastapack (fantastapack.com) covers broad custom-corrugated structures. Crashlock differs by making the structural die-line library and the saved 'pack profile' the core product, so reordering and versioning are first-class, not afterthoughts.
Modern.positioningStatement: Crashlock is the platform where your packaging lives as a saved, reorderable profile across every structural die-line you use.

Modern.tagline: Send it. Send it back. Send it again.
Modern.brandDescription: Returnloop is a returnable, reusable packaging system that replaces single-use mailers and boxes with durable packs that cycle back through a return-and-reuse loop. Returnloop provides the reusable mailers, the QR-coded return logistics, and the tracking dashboard that proves how many cycles each pack completed and how much single-use waste it displaced. It serves brands and closed-loop retailers who want reuse as a measurable, reportable sustainability lever rather than a pilot.
Modern.scope: A reuse-as-a-service platform: durable reusable mailers and totes, reverse-logistics return flows, cleaning/redistribution, and per-pack cycle reporting. Returnloop manages the loop; it does not sell single-use packaging.
Modern.brandNameRationale: The return loop is the literal reverse-logistics cycle a reusable pack travels, and 'loop' is the established term in circular-packaging systems. Returnloop names the cycle the whole product is built around.
Modern.industrySummary: Reusable packaging moved from pilot to procurement line item in 2025 as EU PPWR set binding reuse targets for transport and e-commerce packaging and several retailers committed to reuse percentages. The hard problem is return rate: systems only pay off above a threshold number of cycles, so QR tracking, deposit/incentive design and reverse logistics are the real product. PFAS and plastic-tax pressure also push brands toward durable reuse over disposable plastic film. The opening is a reuse system that makes cycle counts and waste-avoided auditable.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Returnity (returnity.co) is the leading reusable-shipping system for retailers and enterprises. RePack (repack.com) pioneered returnable e-commerce mailers in Europe with a deposit model. Olive built a consumer-facing reusable-shipping aggregation play. Returnloop differs by making per-pack cycle data and waste-avoided reporting the headline product, so sustainability teams can publish verified loop metrics.
Modern.positioningStatement: Returnloop is the reusable packaging system that proves every cycle, so reuse becomes a reportable metric.
Modern.positioningRationale: Reuse only works financially and environmentally above a cycle threshold, and brands struggle to prove it. By instrumenting each pack with QR tracking and publishing cycle and waste-avoided data, Returnloop turns reuse from a feel-good pilot into an audited number. That auditability wins enterprise sustainability buyers.

Modern.tagline: Structure and story for the brands you unbox.
Modern.brandDescription: Dieline Studio is a packaging-design studio for D2C brands that designs both the structure and the surface — the die-line and the artwork — as one system. Dieline Studio takes a brand from napkin sketch to dielocked, press-ready files, handling structural engineering, finish specs, mockups and supplier handoff. It is the design partner for founders who want their packaging to look intentional and actually run on press without surprises.
Modern.scope: Packaging design services: structural die-line engineering, surface/graphic design, finish and substrate specification, prototyping, and production-ready file handoff to printers. Dieline Studio designs packaging; it does not manufacture or print it.
Modern.brandNameRationale: The die-line is the flat cut-and-crease template that defines a package's structure — the single most important file in packaging design. Naming the studio after it claims the discipline at its root.
Modern.industrySummary: As D2C brands matured, packaging design split from generic graphic design into a specialist craft combining structural engineering with surface art, because a beautiful comp that ignores the die-line dies on press. The unboxing-experience economy raised the bar for inserts, reveals and finish, while EPR and right-sizing pressure forced designers to optimize structure for material and dimensional efficiency. Brands increasingly want one partner who owns both the die-line and the artwork through to a press-ready handoff. The opening is a studio that names and centers the die-line.
Modern.competitorLandscape: noissue (noissue.co) bundles design tooling with its own production but is template-led. Packlane (packlane.com) offers design help inside a product configurator. Independent studios like Smith & Diction take packaging projects within broader branding work. Dieline Studio differs by being a structure-and-surface specialist that hands off press-ready files to any printer, keeping the brand's supplier choice open.
Modern.positioningStatement: Dieline Studio is the packaging-design partner that owns structure and surface together, all the way to press-ready files.
Modern.positioningRationale: Brands get burned when graphic designers ignore structure or printers redraw weak die-lines. By owning both disciplines and the handoff, Dieline Studio removes the gap where packaging projects fail. That end-to-end ownership is the value, and it stays printer-agnostic so the brand keeps leverage.

Luxury.tagline: The box that holds the gift it equals.
Luxury.brandDescription: Maison Rigide is a luxury rigid-box maker for jewelry, watch and prestige-cosmetics houses, crafting set-up boxes wrapped in fine papers, lined in silk and magnet-closed with a satisfying weight. Maison Rigide treats the box as part of the object — turned edges, debossed lids, and tolerances measured to the millimeter. It supplies maisons that understand the box is the first thing a client touches and the last thing they keep.
Luxury.scope: Bespoke and short-run rigid (set-up) box manufacturing: paper wrapping, lining, magnetic and ribbon closures, foil, deboss and structural inserts for jewelry, watch and luxury beauty clients. Maison Rigide makes presentation boxes, not shipping cartons or folding cartons.

Luxury.industrySummary: Luxury rigid-box making sits apart from mainstream packaging: it is labor-intensive, low-volume, and judged on hand-finish — turned edges, lining fit, and lid-to-base tolerance. In 2025 even prestige houses face sustainability scrutiny, driving a shift to FSC greyboard, paper-based magnet alternatives and recyclable foils without sacrificing weight and feel. Reusability has become a quiet luxury value as clients keep and display the box. The opening is a maker that frames rigid construction as the object itself.
Luxury.competitorLandscape: Progress Packaging (progresspackaging.co.uk) is a leading creative luxury packaging maker for fashion and beauty houses. Delta Global (deltaglobal.io) supplies sustainable luxury packaging to global brands at scale. Taylor Box brings heritage American set-up box craft. Maison Rigide differs by positioning itself as a small, maison-grade atelier obsessed with turned-edge finish and lid tolerance for jewelry and watches specifically.
Luxury.positioningStatement: Maison Rigide is the atelier that makes the rigid box a luxury object in its own right.
Luxury.positioningRationale: At the prestige tier, clients judge a house partly by the box, yet most suppliers chase volume over finish. By staying small and obsessing over turned edges, lining and tolerance, Maison Rigide serves maisons who will pay for hand-finish. That craft focus is the differentiator.

Creative.tagline: Zine-style packaging you'll want to keep and read.
Creative.brandDescription: Zine & Score is a zine-style product packaging studio that designs packaging as a little publication — folded, scored, stapled or perforated packs that read like a self-published zine. Zine & Score brings cut-and-paste, photocopy and DIY aesthetics to product packaging and inserts, making the pack itself a piece of editorial worth keeping. It is the studio for brands who want their packaging to feel like a zine pulled from a record-shop rack.
Creative.scope: Zine-style packaging and inserts: folded and scored packs, booklet inserts, perforated and stapled formats with cut-and-paste, editorial and DIY aesthetics. Zine & Score designs packaging; production runs through the client's printers and finishers.
Creative.brandNameRationale: A zine is the self-published booklet aesthetic the studio channels, and a score is the crease line that lets paper fold cleanly. Zine & Score pairs the editorial format with the structural fold that makes packaging behave like a publication.
Creative.industrySummary: Zine and DIY aesthetics have re-entered mainstream design as brands seek authenticity, counterculture credibility and a tactile, keep-worthy quality that slick packaging lacks. Treating packaging and inserts as editorial — booklets, folded zines, perforated cards — extends dwell time and builds community feeling, performing well in the unboxing economy. Riso, photocopy and uncoated stocks reinforce the handmade, low-impact feel. The opening is a studio that designs packaging as a zine-like publication.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Zine-and-editorial design studios exist but rarely focus on packaging structure. noissue (noissue.co) prints custom packaging but in conventional formats. Riso studios print zines but not as packaging. Zine & Score differs by specializing in packaging that behaves like a zine — scored, folded and editorial — bringing publication craft to the pack itself.
Creative.positioningStatement: Zine & Score is the studio that designs packaging to read and keep like a self-published zine.
Creative.positioningRationale: Brands chasing authenticity and dwell time want packaging that feels handmade and editorial rather than slick and disposable. Creative.tagline: Playful labels for the good little batches.
Creative.brandDescription: Small Batch Laydown is a playful small-batch label studio designing characterful labels for makers — jams, hot sauces, candles, kombucha, coffee — who produce in real small batches and want labels with personality. Small Batch Laydown creates illustrated, hand-lettered, color-popping labels and the laydown artwork ready for short-run print, celebrating the maker behind each batch. It is the label studio for small producers who refuse to look mass-produced.
Creative.scope: Small-batch label design: illustrated and hand-lettered labels, batch and variant systems, and print-ready laydown artwork for food, drink and craft makers. Small Batch Laydown designs labels; printing runs through short-run label printers.
Creative.brandNameRationale: A laydown is the flat artwork before it's applied, and 'small batch' names the maker's scale. Small Batch Laydown pairs the print-artwork term with the small-producer ethos it serves, distinct from the modern mailer brand by its label-and-maker focus.
Creative.industrySummary: Small-batch and craft makers have proliferated across food, drink and home categories, and they compete on personality and authenticity where a characterful label is the primary brand asset. Short-run digital label printing makes it affordable to print small quantities and many variants, enabling playful, batch-specific designs. The maker-economy and farmers-market-to-shelf pipeline rewards labels that signal handmade craft. The opening is a studio specializing in playful, characterful labels for genuine small-batch producers.
Creative.competitorLandscape: noissue (noissue.co) prints custom labels for makers but in templated formats. Avery WePrint (avery.com) offers short-run custom labels broadly. Online tools like Canva (canva.com) let makers DIY labels generically. Small Batch Laydown differs by specializing in playful, illustrated, batch-aware label design for small makers, delivering print-ready laydown artwork that celebrates the maker behind each batch.
Creative.positioningStatement: Small Batch Laydown is the label studio that gives small-batch makers labels as characterful as their craft.
Creative.positioningRationale: Small makers live or die by shelf personality, and generic DIY labels make great products look mass-produced. By specializing in playful, batch-aware labels with print-ready artwork, Small Batch Laydown gives makers a distinctive, affordable brand asset. That maker-focused playfulness is the differentiator.

targetAudience.primary: Makers and small founders producing food, drink and craft goods in genuine small batches who want characterful labels that match their craft and don't look generic. They value personality, affordability and batch flexibility, and sell at markets, online and in indie shops. They commission per product and add variants and batches over time.
